## Natural history notes

A tiny leaf-mining moth characterized by its very small size, narrow pale silvery-white wings, and delicate fringed wing edges typical of gracillariid moths. In Florida, it is found in open and disturbed habitats such as fields, roadsides, gardens, weedy edges, and parks where aster-family host plants occur. Adults are easily overlooked and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed inside leaves of plants such as American burnweed and butterweed, forming long, winding mines between the leaf surfaces as they develop.
